statements.attributed: provides the atomic sphere approximation for modeling atomic potentials
statements.quote: The atomic potentials were modeled within the atomic sphere approximation, supplemented by a variationally optimized potential energy zero, resulting in formation energies matching full potential results. The valence states were expanded in a spherical harmonic basis that included angular momentum up to lmax = 5 (i.e., electron symmetries of s, p, d, and f electrons).

statements.quote: As it approaches singularity when the energies approach the Fermi level (εF), two Monkhorst–Pack (MP) k-point meshes were used.

statements.attributed: provides the Super-Cell Random Approximates (SCRAPs) method
statements.quote: The large bulk supercell was generated using the Super-Cell Random Approximates (SCRAPs) method by Johnson and co-workers and calculated using VASP.

statements.attributed: provides the projector augmented wave method for describing core electron potentials
statements.quote: The potentials due to the core electrons were described using the projector augmented wave method. The Kohn–Sham one-electron valence states [Cr(3p3d4s), Fe(3d4s), Co(3d4s), Ni(3d4s), O(2s2p), and H(1s)] were expanded in a plane-wave basis up to 650 eV.

statements.attributed: provides the method for separating periodic slabs with vacuum and applying electrostatic decoupling
statements.quote: Periodic slabs were separated in the z-direction by five layers equivalent of vacuum, with electrostatic decoupling applied in the z-direction. The surface Brillouin zone was sampled on a 2 × 2 × 1 MP k-point mesh for each surface unit cell.

statements.attributed: provides the first-order Methfessel–Paxton scheme for smearing electronic states
statements.quote: A first-order Methfessel–Paxton scheme was used to smear the electronic states with a width of 0.2. All total energies were extrapolated to 0 K.

statements.attributed: defines the free energy corrections (δG) to the total energies for adsorbed atomic H and O and for gas-phase molecular H2
statements.quote: See ref for how the free energy corrections (δG) to the total energies are defined for adsorbed atomic H and O (δGA*(T)) and for gas-phase molecular H2 (δGH2(g)(T,p)). δGO2(g)(T,p) was calculated using the approach of Martínez et al. to avoid the error inherent in the GGA total energy of gas-phase O2. At ambient temperature and pressure (298.15 K and 1 bar), ΔΔG was estimated to be 0.21 eV (in agreement with Nørskov et al.) and 0.13 eV per adsorbed H and O atom, respectively.
